card.stem: The sketch shows portion of the eaves of a pitched roof. The slated cut roof has a pitch of 30°. The roof is supported on a 400 mm concrete block wall with a full-fill insulated cavity. The slates are fixed to 50 mm × 30 mm battens, on a breather membrane, supported on 200 mm × 50 mm rafters. The ceiling joists are 200 mm × 50 mm with plasterboard fixed beneath. The roof is highly insulated at ceiling joist level.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:5, draw a vertical section through the external wall and through the eaves of the pitched roof. On your drawing, show the typical construction details from a level 400 mm below the wallplate, through the wall and eaves. Include the first three courses of slate at eaves. Include three typical dimensions on your drawing.

rows.contextNote: Any 7 x 5 marks. Credit the best SEVEN acceptable details at 5 marks each, capped at 35. Marked details: slates on 50 × 30 mm battens; breather membrane; rafters 200 × 50 mm; ceiling joists with insulation between; insulated plasterboard with skim; wallplate 100 × 75 mm; airtight membrane and tape; ventilation; tilting fillet, fascia, soffit and gutter; block inner leaf; 200 mm full-fill cavity with ties and cavity closer; block outer leaf; 13 mm plaster and 19 mm render.

options: Ceiling joist with insulation between joists
Tilting fillet, fascia, soffit and eaves gutter
13 mm internal plaster and 19 mm render

rows.contextNote: Three appropriate typical dimensions on the section.

rows.verbatim: Draughting, accuracy and scale (excellent, good, fair)
rows.contextNote: Draughting, accuracy and scale of the section: excellent 8, good 6, fair 4.

card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and freehand sketches, any five of the following: joist bridging; steel reinforcement; biscuit joint; working drawing; heat pump; room thermostat; rooflight; ridgeboard; building energy rating.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Joist bridging: keeps floor joists vertical and stops them twisting; stiffens and ties the joists together and spreads load to neighbouring joists; solid or herringbone bridging. Steel reinforcement: combined with concrete as reinforced concrete, taking the tension in load-bearing members; placed low in a foundation; patterned bars (rebar) or mesh for grip, tied into cages. Biscuit joint: used in modern furniture for butt and edge joints in boards of different widths and thicknesses; pressed beech biscuits fit grooves cut by a biscuit joiner, giving a larger gluing area. Working drawing: a scaled drawing used as a guide when building furniture or buildings, with elevations, plan and sections, dimensions and notes; hand drafted or CAD; often called plans or blueprints. Heat pump: moves heat from one place to another, such as from the outside air or ground into the house for heating and hot water, very efficiently. Room thermostat: senses the room temperature and switches the heating to keep it at the chosen level; dial, digital or smart (Wi-Fi) control; lower heating bills and less waste. Roof light: a window in the roof surface for natural light, double, triple or quadruple glazed; lets an attic become a usable room; more privacy than a dormer. Ridge board: the horizontal member at the top ends of the rafters forming the apex of a cut roof; rafters are nailed to it; supported by the rafters or gables; typically 225 × 32 or 225 × 25 mm. Building Energy Rating: a certificate rating a home’s energy performance from A to G, calculated on the energy for space heating, hot water, ventilation and lighting; A is the most efficient with the lowest bills.
